# Chipline

> Chipline is a free online five-in-a-row card board game, in the style of Sequence, for 2 to 12 players. Play in the browser with friends on different phones, against computer players, or pass-and-play on one device. No download or sign-up.

Key facts:
- Price: free. Runs in any web browser on phones, tablets and computers. No download, no account.
- Players: 2 to 12, solo against the computer, or in 2 or 3 teams.
- Modes: online rooms with an invite link or 5-letter code, play against the computer, pass one phone around.
- Online extras: computer players can fill empty seats, a turn timer (30, 60 or 90 seconds), and a computer takes over if someone leaves.
- Rules in short: play a card, place your team's chip on the matching board space; two-eyed jacks are wild, one-eyed jacks remove an opponent chip; the four corners are free; two teams need two lines of five, three teams need one.
- Chipline is an independent game and is not affiliated with the makers of the Sequence board game.

- [Sequence game rules, explained simply](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/rules/): setup, turns, jacks, corners, dead cards, how to win, and rules for 2, 3, 4 players and teams
- [Play board games online with friends](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/play-with-friends/): how to start a room, share the link on WhatsApp, player counts and teams, turn timer, computer players, and what happens if someone drops out
- [Play Sequence against the computer](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/vs-computer/): one-tap solo games, how the computer player plays, tips to beat it, and mixing people with computer players

- [Sequence strategy tips](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/strategy/): 12 tips on blocking, jacks, corners, double threats and team play.
- [Sequence FAQ](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/faq/): short answers on cards, players, jacks, corners, dead cards and winning.
- [One-page rules sheet (PDF)](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/sequence-rules.pdf): printable summary of the rules.
- [Sequence rules for 2 players](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/sequence-rules-for-2-players/): how to play head-to-head with 7 cards each and two sequences to win, plus 2-player strategy.
- [Jokers in Sequence](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/jokers-in-sequence-game/): jokers are not used in standard Sequence; why the box includes them, which jacks are wild instead, and optional house rules for jokers.
- [Sequence rules for 4 players](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/sequence-game-rules-4-players/): four players play as 2 teams of 2 with 6 cards each and need two sequences to win; seating, turns, jacks and team strategy.
- [Sequence game board layout](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/sequence-game-board-layout/): the 10x10 board has 100 spaces, with every card except the jacks shown twice plus 4 free corners; why jacks are left off, how corners work, and how to make your own board.
- [Games like Sequence](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/games-like-sequence/): 8 alternatives such as Gomoku, Pente, Connect Four, Qwirkle, Blokus and Rummikub compared by players, luck and strategy, and how to play a Sequence-style game free online.
- [Sequence dead card rules](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/sequence-dead-card-rules/): a dead card has both board spaces covered; swap one per turn by discarding it, announcing it and drawing a replacement before you play, plus edge cases and dead card strategy.
- [How many cards are in Sequence?](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/how-many-cards-in-sequence/): Sequence uses 104 cards (two standard decks, no jokers); players get 7 cards with 2 players, 6 with 3 or 4, 5 with 6, 4 with 8 or 9, and 3 with 10 or 12, plus how dealing, drawing and an empty draw pile work.
- [What is Sequence?](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/what-is-sequence-game/): Sequence is a card-and-board game where you play a card to place a chip on its matching space of a 10x10 board and race to make rows of five; covers the board, jacks, how to win, luck vs skill and player counts.
- [Sequence game for kids](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/sequence-game-for-kids/): the game is usually labeled ages 7 and up, younger kids can play on a team with an adult; how to teach it step by step, explain the jacks, and kid-friendly house rules.
- [Sequence game corner rules](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/sequence-game-corner-rules/): the four corners are free spaces that count as a chip for every player or team, so a line through a corner needs only four chips; nobody places chips there, jacks cannot affect them, and a corner can be the one shared space between two sequences.
- [Sequence game with playing cards](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/sequence-game-with-playing-cards/): you can play Sequence with four standard decks, two (jacks and jokers removed) laid out as the 10x10 board with free corners and two as the 104-card draw pile; covers setup, hand sizes, which jacks are wild and pitfalls of a homemade board.
- [Sequence game app](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/sequence-game-app/): you can play Sequence on a phone with a downloaded app or free in the browser with no download; compares apps vs browser games, explains adding a game to the home screen, what a good app needs, and playing with friends on iPhone and Android together.
- [How many sequences do you need to win?](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/how-many-sequences-to-win/): two sides (2 players or 2 teams) need two sequences of five and three sides need one; covers a table for every player count, the rule that two sequences may share one chip, corners, why finished sequences are safe from one-eyed jacks, and tips.
- [Blog](https://playsequenceonline.github.io/blog/): guides such as rules for 3 players, one-eyed vs two-eyed jacks, and playing with 6 to 12 players
